Strength is split by search only: training and validation rows take a strength score fitted without their search fold but WITH their own site's pages on other searches (later ones too), and test rows the main score, fitted on training pages before the cutoff that hold held-out sites on training searches; strength_own_site_in_fit counts them. later_labels counts rows whose models learned from pages dated after the row's forecast date (none for test rows).

new_to_search_rule.origin: The idea of a separate rule for sites new to the search comes from the version 1 held-out result: on those sites the updater scored 0.820 against 0.867 for always NOT IN TOP 50. The rule itself is chosen on validation rows only.
new_to_search_rule.rule: on the segment's validation rows, the version in use stays unless a candidate (always NT50, the table, the model) beats it with a cluster interval over searches whose lower bound is above zero; among those the largest gain wins
new_to_search_rule.why: always_nt50 beat the version in use (model) on 12445 validation rows of the segment with a lower bound above 0.0
